title: Dragons: As Real as Mermaids
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the origins and history of dragons across cultures. They discuss how every culture having dragons is partly a product of translation and overlay, David E. Jones's theory that humans fear snakes, cats and eagles, the swarm-of-bees theory, and the Greek word drakon originally meaning snake. They cover Sumerian and Akkadian dragon-like beings, Revelation's dragon as Satan, Beowulf's dragon, the St. George and Theodore dragon legends (possibly a crocodile at a spring), the medieval Harley manuscript dragon image, benevolent Asian rain dragons (long), Chen Rong's thirteenth-century dragon paintings, and famous dragons in literature, games and film. A listener mail about corn in a childhood poop story closes the episode.
topics: David E. Jones An Instinct for Dragons

segments.title: Opening banter and dragon setup
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about Bill Withers and George Benson, then introduce the episode on dragons and its tie-in to the Mermaids selects episode. They note that dragon types differ between Western and Asian traditions.

segments.title: Fear of predators and the bee swarm theory
segments.summary: They discuss David E. Jones's theory that humans fear snakes, cats and eagles, which combined into the dragon, and the speculative theory that bee swarms, honey and bee stings inspired dragon imagery. Folklore explaining fossils is also mentioned.
topics: David E. Jones An Instinct for Dragons

segments.title: Drakon as a word for snake
segments.summary: They explain that the Greek word drakon originally meant snake, as Homer used it, and that later writers and natural histories applied it to varied snakes and exaggerated creatures.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Short break with banter about Ned Flanders.

segments.title: Mistranslation and Sumerian dragons
segments.summary: They discuss how classical writers mixed natural history and myth, and how lazy translation turned many mythical beasts into dragons. Sumerian mu-sum beings and Akkadian scholarship are covered.

segments.title: Revelation, Satan and Western dragon tales
segments.summary: They cover the dragon in Revelation as Satan, Paradise Lost, and the Beowulf dragon guarding treasure. St. George and St. Theodore dragon legends are introduced, including a possible crocodile at a spring in Anatolia.

segments.title: Medieval dragon imagery and Asian dragons
segments.summary: They describe the 1268 Harley bestiary illustration by William Perrault as an early Western dragon image, then turn to benevolent Asian rain dragons (long), animism, and Chinese dragon jade figures.

segments.title: Chen Rong, Japanese dragons and famous dragons
segments.summary: They discuss Chen Rong's thirteenth-century dragon paintings, Japanese dragons in the video game Ghost of Tsushima, and famous dragons from Tolkien, Dungeons and Dragons, Reign of Fire, Pete's Dragon, Puff the Magic Dragon and Dragon Ball Z.

segments.title: Listener mail: corn and poop story
segments.summary: Listener Mary from Issaquah, Washington shares a childhood story about corn appearing in a neighbor child's diaper in Houston, and thanks the hosts.
